no: From Angel Montesdeoca, February 28, 2020: Let ℰ _a be the ellipse with major axis the segment BC and length of the minor axis a/\(\sqrt{3}\). Let L_{a} be the polar of A wrt ℰ _a, and define L_{b} and L_{c} cyclically. Let A' = L_{b} ∩ L_{c}, B' = L_{c} ∩ L_{a}, C' = L_{a} ∩ L_{b}. The lines AA', BB', CC' concur in X_14491. A barycentric equation for the ellipse ℰ _a: 2 \(a^{4}\) \(x^{2}\) + \(a^{4}\) x y+ \(a^{4}\) x z+2 \(a^{4}\) y z-3 \(a^{2}\) \(b^{2}\) \(x^{2}\)-\(a^{2}\) \(b^{2}\) x y+ \(a^{2}\) \(b^{2}\) x z-3 \(a^{2}\) \(c^{2}\) \(x^{2}\) + \(a^{2}\) \(c^{2}\) x y-\(a^{2}\) \(c^{2}\) x z+ \(b^{4}\) \(x^{2}\)-2 \(b^{2}\) \(c^{2}\) \(x^{2}\) + \(c^{4}\) \(x^{2}\) =0.
